goal: Make me a practical Python lab for running small language-model fine-tuning experiments reproducibly. I want to define an experiment, validate conversational training data and its train/evaluation separation, save the resolved configuration, run a short training smoke through a replaceable trainer, save its adapter and metadata, evaluate the starting model and candidate under matched settings, and get a readable before/after summary. A malformed dataset or overlapping held-out examples should stop preflight rather than quietly train. Keep experiment runs in separate directories, preserve older outputs, and record model/data revisions, seed, code identity and effective settings so I can tell what actually ran. If a run fails, retain its logs and status without claiming success. Do not require a GPU, download weights or start real training when I run the lab's own tests: use a tiny fake trainer/evaluator there, but make the workflow ready to connect to a real backend. Keep credentials and large weights out of manifests and Git, distinguish unavailable metrics from zeros, and give me simple commands for preparing, running and comparing one experiment.

tasks.title: Specify conversation/split validation before any backend is invoked.
acceptance: Reject empty messages, wrong roles, unknown splits and normalized overlapping prompts.
The trainer is never invoked after invalid preflight.

tasks.title: Specify train/test routing and reproducible matched model comparisons.
acceptance: Trainer receives only training rows and evaluator only test rows.
Baseline identity is the model revision and candidate identity the adapter path.
Preserve resolved config, adapter and completed status.
Report real deltas and unavailable metrics without replacing missingness with zero.

tasks.title: Specify immutable previous runs and faithful zero-valued metrics.
acceptance: A distinct run succeeds without modifying any previous file bytes.

tasks.title: Specify explicit failed status and secret-free returned and saved errors.
acceptance: Backend failure yields failed status, useful diagnostics and no success summary.
Configured secret values are absent from returned errors and every saved text artifact.

acceptance: Real training backend integration, credential publishing policy and actual CLI delivery remain separate checks.
